mix_frequency_estimate: AJ-overcard-BDFD-Ax-blocker class facing 25% donk/cbet 4-way SRP with 2 players behind: FOLD 65% / CALL 35%. AhJh combo (Ah-blocker, no straight equity): FOLD 60% / CALL 40%.
reasoning:
Node identity: hero MP/HJ (data field hero_position=HJ; preflop action labels hero MP — minor data inconsistency, treat as 'early-to-middle position with CO and BTN behind'), facing UTG cbet of 2.5bb into pot 12.5bb. Hero is NOT closing action — CO and BTN are behind and will see hero's call as 'hero called UTG's small bet, with two unknowns left to act'.

Pot odds: 2.5 to win 15 → 16.7% required equity.

Hand strength: AhJh on 3h7c5d.
  - 6 overcard outs (any A or J pairs hero, but DIRTY — top pair Aces or Jx is medium-strength on this board, can lose to set/two pair/PFA's overpair).
  - BDFD: 3 hearts (Ah+Jh+3h) = backdoor flush draw, ~1.5 outs equivalent over two streets.
  - No straight draw: A-J + 3-5-7 — too disconnected.
  - Ah-blocker: blocks UTG's AhKh, AhQh, AhTh nut FD combos. Important for raw equity vs UTG cbet range.

Equity calculation vs UTG cbet range:
  - UTG opens UTG-wide range (TT-22, ATs+, KQs, suited connectors, suited Ax). Cbets 4-way SRP — narrows to value (TPTK+, overpair, set) and FD/strong-draws. Tighter cbet range than wider open range.
  - Range: ~AA-77 (overpair sometimes), 77/55/33 (sets), A7/A5/A3 (TPGK-class), suited 7x with FD/SD, ATs-AKs with BDFD.
  - vs this range, AhJh has ~28-32% equity by river. Realization is ~0.8 IP-against-PFA (hero is IP relative to UTG since UTG acts first postflop) — call this realized equity ~24-26%.

Pot odds 16.7% < realized equity 24-26%. CALL is mathematically defensible.

BUT FOUR CONSIDERATIONS PUSH TOWARD FOLD:
  (1) Two players behind (CO, BTN) — call-then-raise risk. If CO/BTN flat behind, hero plays 4-way turn with weak overcards; if one raises, hero must fold. The squeeze probability is ~15-20%. This reduces effective implied odds and increases reverse implied odds.
  (2) Multiway-realization OOP-vs-3-implicit: even though UTG is OOP relative to hero, having two callers behind degrades hero's IP-leverage. Realization drops to ~0.7 effective.
  (3) Dirty overcards: pairing the A or J does NOT guarantee best hand in MW. UTG cbet range has AT/AJ/AQ/AK that beat AJ on an A turn (hero's Jh kicker is weak vs AK/AQ). Pairing the J is even dirtier (loses to AA-99 overpair, JT/JJ).
  (4) Closing-action axis (per primary_axis 'TPTK-MP-early-action-MW') suggests this variant family is centered on positions where the hero's call locks in a tough turn. The 'MP-early-action' classification confirms hero is NOT closing — CO/BTN behind to act — which is the WORST position for a thin overcard-BDFD call.

COUNTER (CALL argument):
  - Realized equity ~24-26% > pot odds 16.7% suggests a +EV call on raw equity.
  - Ah-blocker has real value: blocks UTG's strongest cbet combos (AhKh, AhQh, AhTh).
  - Implied odds OK if hero hits an A (vs UTG's TT-77, KQs, suited connectors) — those pay off TPTK on Ax turn.
  - Calling preserves CO/BTN squeeze-target, but the squeeze is also rare (only ~15-20% of pots).

The spot is genuinely close. The screening report's corrected equity estimate of 28-33% is at the high end of my calculation; using 28% as the equity floor, CALL becomes more defensible. Using 24-26% realized, FOLD becomes more defensible.

Class-level frequency: AJ-overcard-BDFD with A-blocker facing small donk-cbet in MW SRP with players behind: SOLVER tendency on similar nodes is a mix FOLD 55-65% / CALL 35-45%. The combo with strong Ah-blocker (AhJh) shifts slightly toward CALL within the class (Ah-blocker reduces UTG's strongest combos), so AhJh lands at ~40% CALL / 60% FOLD.

Verdict: FOLD at MEDIUM confidence (marginal). The consensus FOLD is the modal action, but the CALL frequency is non-trivial (~40% for AhJh specifically). I AGREE with consensus on the action label but note the margin is thin and a small (~5-10%) shift in equity assumption could flip the modal action.
